alias-hop-bound (endpoint and callee alias chains of 16 or more hops)
checked_another_way: same-line-neighbour and same-line-declaring-neighbour: they only withhold a verdict, as UNDECIDED endpoint-coordinate-off; counted from the verdict files instead of the script: 0 rows with that reason on Express and 0 on whole Excalidraw

limits.title: A claim to the formal of a body-less signature (interface method, call, construct, index or accessor signature, abstract method or setter) while the call is to another function
limits.note: The claimed destination emits no JavaScript and the call goes to another function. Controls: calls that do reach a signature are UNDECIDED type-only-declaration (judged correctly); the same call to a function with a body is CORRECT. Rows 6 and 10 (a call to `s.m` or `abs.am` claimed to the index signature and to the setter) are UNDECIDED type-only-declaration too: no call reaches those two formals, the verdict is right because the call resolves to another body-less declaration.

limits.title: A claim to a signature formal of an overloaded function that has one implementation
limits.note: Documented exception, not a grader defect: with one implementation either overload signature formal is WRONG implementation-slot and the implementation formal is CORRECT (oracle-032, oracle-037). A strict reading of the scope (a body-less signature emits nothing) would make both UNDECIDED; the exception is kept because the claim names a slot that is provably not the implementation. With no implementation both are UNDECIDED type-only-declaration. The pinned example is a function; method and constructor overloads follow the same rule (README argument-fold7 rows).

limits.title: An import that reaches a value only through `export type *`, alone or forwarded by a named re-export
limits.note: The `export type *` mark sits on the export declaration, not on a symbol the alias walk reads (probable cause, not proved). Controls: a live import is CORRECT; `import type` and an interface imported by name are UNDECIDED.

limits.title: A call whose callee is reached through `import type { fn }` or a type-only star: the argument is credited against the callee formal although TS1361/TS1362 reject the value use
limits.note: The callable proof does not apply the type-only provenance rule. Control: the same call through an ordinary import is CORRECT.

limits.title: A live import through a long chain of named re-exports is withheld (the alias walk stops after 16 hops, a fixed bound of judged_scope.cjs, not a property of the program)
limits.note: The 16-hop bound is an implementation cap: the import-to-read row of a 16-link chain is UNDECIDED outside-judged-scope while the 7-link chain is CORRECT. In this program the call row through the long chain stays CORRECT (the callable proof has no such bound); sol saw it withheld in its own program and that was not reproduced.

limits.title: Code a const enum, a folded enum initializer or a namespace holding only const enums erases (receiver `N.E.A` and `N["E"]["A"]`)
limits.note: TypeScript emits neither the namespace nor the read, or replaces the read with its constant. Controls: an instantiated namespace and a plain read of the same constant are CORRECT.

limits.title: A literal actual in a computed key that is erased (interface, type literal, ambient class, abstract method)
limits.note: The literal path skips the evaluated-context check. Control: the same call outside any erased key is CORRECT.

limits.title: An identifier read nested in an erased computed key (`key({ v })` in an interface, `key(() => v)` in an abstract method)
limits.note: The ancestor walk of the erased-key check stops at the nearest expression. Control: `key({ v })` outside any erased key is CORRECT.

limits.title: `(id)<number>`, `((id))<number>`, `(cond ? id : other)<number>` and a bare `id<number>`: the value is read, the type arguments are not
limits.note: The role classifier takes the operand for a type position (WRONG type-position) or, for a bare operand, withholds it (outside-judged-scope). Required verdict is CORRECT. Control: `id(1)` is CORRECT.

limits.title: A same-line neighbour that cannot serve the claimed role (a member read, a label) withholds a proved contradiction
limits.note: The neighbour check counts a token that cannot serve the claimed edge (`obj.x`, a label `z:`). Today UNDECIDED endpoint-coordinate-off; the stated rule requires the WRONG the control gets.

limits.title: Two same-line named class expressions, regular enums or function expressions: a cross-binding edge is UNDECIDED
limits.source: sol r2, closure; Opus r2 finding 2
limits.note: Not a defect: the same-line neighbour declares the very binding that the read resolves to, so it can serve the role and the position is coordinate-uncertain. The required verdict is UNDECIDED, the same as today (the earlier draft required WRONG different-declaration; the safer reading is kept because a producer anchors an endpoint by line). Controls: the same programs with the declarations on separate lines are WRONG different-declaration. Instantiated namespaces: both the same-line row and the control are UNDECIDED declaration-unproved (not reproduced, not pinned).

limits.title: A name with no checker symbol (an undeclared global) passes the value test and receives a role-fault WRONG
limits.note: Scope condition 4 admits a name that has no symbol, so the WRONG write-position is the scope working as stated, and it is true about the edge (a write marked as a read destination). Required verdict equals today. Opus also reproduced it with a type alias used as a value, which does not compile. Census: 0 symbol-less endpoints among decided rows. Control: the same shape on a declared variable.
